mainTopic: Does a second נזירות (or a second שבועה) take effect on top of the first? The גמרא challenges רב הונא from our משנה, from רבה, and from a ברייתא about two נזירות.
overview: The amud opens by ending an earlier challenge to רב הונא, which stays a קשיא (a difficulty, not a full refutation). Then the גמרא challenges him from our משנה: 'יש נדר בתוך נדר, ואין שבועה בתוך שבועה.' If the משנה meant two different נזירות periods ('today, tomorrow'), the matching oath case would be two different foods, and both oaths would take effect. So it seems the משנה means the same words said twice, and it says a repeated נזירות does take effect, which goes against רב הונא. רב הונא answers that the משנה does mean 'today, tomorrow'. The matching oath case is an overlapping oath ('figs', then 'figs and grapes'), which does not take effect. The גמרא pushes back with רבה's ruling: because of a מיגו, such an overlapping oath takes effect even on the figs. The answer is that רב הונא does not hold like רבה. Finally the גמרא brings a ברייתא about two נזירות and shows that its case must be 'נזיר today' said twice. The challenge this raises against רב הונא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The previous challenge to רב הונא stays a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends a previous challenge against רב הונא by saying that in that case there is no vow within a vow, and calls it a קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no vow within a vow! This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier challenge to רב הונא. It labels it 'קשיא', a real difficulty left without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קשיא' at the end of a challenge means the problem is not solved. It is not the stronger word 'תיובתא', which would mean full refutation. So רב הונא's view is under pressure, but it has not been thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow within a vow: a second vow taking effect on top of a first one
A difficulty: an unanswered question, but not a full refutation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'קשיא' as 'רב הונא is wrong.' It only means the question stays open. A full refutation would be called 'תיובתא'.

phrases.english: There is no vow within a vow!
It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a challenge that began on the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The earlier challenge to רב הונא is left as an unresolved difficulty, not a full refutation.

steps.title: Quoting our משנה: a vow within a vow, but no oath within an oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a vow can take effect on top of a vow, but an oath cannot take effect on top of an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: There is a vow within a vow, but there is no oath within an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from our משנה. This sets up a new challenge to רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts נדר and שבועה. A second נדר can take effect on top of a first, but a second שבועה cannot. The גמרא will now ask what exact case the משנה means. The answer decides whether the משנה argues with רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath within an oath: a second oath taking effect on top of a first

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole back-and-forth that follows depends on how this line of the משנה is understood.

phrases.english: We learned: There is a vow within a vow,
phrases.notes: This is quoted from our משנה earlier in this chapter.

phrases.english: but there is no oath within an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to רב הונא after the previous one ended as a קשיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second vow can take effect on top of a first, but a second oath cannot.

steps.title: What case is the משנה talking about? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case of 'a vow within a vow' is, and first suggests: 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר tomorrow.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it is where he said, 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר tomorrow'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means and offers a first guess: two different נזירות periods. This sets up a test of that guess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'היכי דמי' asks for the exact case. 'אילימא' ('if you say') brings a possible answer that the גמרא usually goes on to reject. The suggestion is two separate נזירות periods that do not overlap.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
If you say: brings a suggestion that will probably be rejected
I am hereby a נזיר: the words used to accept נזירות

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say it is where he said, 'I am hereby a נזיר today,
I am hereby a נזיר tomorrow',

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which exact case the משנה means by 'a vow within a vow'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First suggestion: two different נזירות periods, today and tomorrow.

steps.title: That suggestion fails: the matching oaths would both take effect
steps.stepSummary: If the vow case is 'today, tomorrow', the matching oath case is 'figs' and then 'grapes'. But then why would the second oath not take effect?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the matching case for an oath would be: 'that I will not eat figs,' and then he said again, 'an oath that I will not eat grapes.' Why would an oath not take effect on an oath?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. The matching oath case would be two oaths about different foods, and those obviously both take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's two halves must describe the same kind of case. Two separate נזירות periods match two oaths about separate foods. Oaths about separate things don't overlap at all, so both should work. The משנה's 'no oath within an oath' would then make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The matching case: the parallel situation
Regarding, in the case of
Why?
Takes effect

phrases.english: the matching case regarding an oath would be:
'[an oath] that I will not eat figs',
phrases.notes: The word 'oath' is left out here but assumed, just like in the next line.

phrases.english: and he then said again, 'an oath that I will not eat grapes' —

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי לָא חָלָה שְׁבוּעָה עַל שְׁבוּעָה?
phrases.english: why would an oath not take effect on an oath?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first suggestion by building the matching oath case, and shows it does not fit.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the משנה means two different נזירות periods.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The matching oath case (figs, then grapes) clearly takes effect, so the משנה could not say 'no oath within an oath' about it.

steps.title: So the משנה must mean the same words said twice, which goes against רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The oath case must be 'figs' said twice. So the נזירות case must be 'נזיר today' said twice, and the משנה says that does take effect, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the case where an oath does not take effect on an oath? For example, where he said, 'An oath that I will not eat figs,' and then said again, 'An oath that I will not eat figs.' What is the matching case for נזירות? Where he said, 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר today.' And the משנה teaches that there is a vow within a vow. This is a difficulty for רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה means the very same commitment said twice. Then it shows that the משנה says a repeated נזירות does take effect, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath that does not take effect must be an exact repeat, because the person is already bound. So the parallel נזירות case is also an exact repeat ('today, today'). The משנה says such a vow does take effect. רב הונא holds that a second identical נזירות does not take effect, so the משנה seems to argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: switches to a new explanation after rejecting one
For example, such as
נזירות: the state of being a נזיר
And it (the משנה) teaches

phrases.english: Rather, what is the case
where an oath does not take effect on an oath?
For example, where he said, 'An oath that I will not eat figs',
and he said again, 'An oath that I will not eat figs'.
What is the matching case regarding נזירות?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר הַיּוֹם, הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר הַיּוֹם״,
phrases.english: Where he said, 'I am hereby a נזיר today, I am hereby a נזיר today',
and it teaches that there is a vow within a vow.
This is a difficulty for רב הונא!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֵיכִי דָּמֵי דְּלָא חָלָה שְׁבוּעָה עַל שְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the 'today, tomorrow' reading, the גמרא adopts the 'exact repeat' reading and turns it against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that a second identical נזירות does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The oath case must be an exact repeat, so the parallel vow case is also an exact repeat. The משנה says that one does take effect, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: רב הונא's answer: the משנה means 'today, tomorrow', and the matching oaths overlap
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the משנה means 'today, tomorrow'. The matching oath case is 'figs', then 'figs and grapes', and that second oath does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can tell you: our משנה is where he said, 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר tomorrow.' The matching oath case is where he said, '[An oath] that I will not eat figs,' and then said, 'An oath that I will not eat figs and grapes,' which does not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא goes back to the 'today, tomorrow' reading. He fixes its problem by choosing a different matching oath case, one where the second oath overlaps the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 rejected 'today, tomorrow' because it matched the oath case to figs and then grapes. רב הונא matches it instead to figs, then 'figs and grapes'. That second oath partly covers something already sworn, so it does not take effect. Now the משנה only speaks about different נזירות periods, and it says nothing against רב הונא's view on an exact repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you: introduces how a sage would defend himself
Our משנה
Takes effect (Aramaic)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא escapes the challenge by reading the משנה as two different נזירות periods ('today, tomorrow'). The matching oath case is an overlapping oath ('figs', then 'figs and grapes'), which does not take effect.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same 'today, tomorrow' reading that step 4 rejected. What changed is the matching oath case: not 'figs, then grapes' but 'figs, then figs and grapes'.

phrases.english: רב הונא can say to you:
our משנה is where he said,
'I am hereby a נזיר today, I am hereby a נזיר tomorrow'.
The matching case regarding an oath is where he said:
'[An oath] that I will not eat figs',
and then he said again:
'An oath that I will not eat figs and grapes',
which does not take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by bringing back the 'today, tomorrow' reading of step 3 with a new matching oath case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (אוקימתא) of the משנה and its parallel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'today, tomorrow' reading was thought to match two oaths about separate foods, which would both take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'today, tomorrow' reading matches an overlapping oath (figs, then figs and grapes), which does not take effect. So the משנה does not address an exact repeat of נזירות and does not argue with רב הונא.

steps.title: Challenge from רבה: the 'figs and grapes' oath does take effect on figs
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that a second oath on 'figs and grapes' takes effect on the figs too, because it already takes effect on the grapes. This goes against רב הונא's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבה say: if someone said, 'An oath that I will not eat figs,' and then said, 'An oath that I will not eat figs and grapes,' and he ate figs, set aside a קרבן, and then ate grapes, the grapes are only a half-measure, and you do not bring a קרבן for a half-measure. This shows that when someone makes the oath on figs and then on 'figs and grapes,' since the second oath takes effect on the grapes, it also takes effect on the figs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's answer from Step 6 by quoting a ruling of רבה. רבה's ruling shows that the second oath, 'figs and grapes,' does take effect, even on the figs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, רב הונא said the second oath ('figs and grapes') does not take effect. רבה, however, treats the grapes as only half of the second oath. That only makes sense if the second oath took hold on the figs as well, through a מיגו: since it takes hold on the grapes, it takes hold on the figs too.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (so-and-so) say? This introduces a statement that seems to contradict what was just said.
Half a measure, less than the full amount that makes a person liable.
He set aside an animal to be his offering.
Apparently, this shows that.
Since. Because it works in one way, it also works in another.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get thrown by the words 'half-measure.' רבה is not saying he ate a small amount of grapes. He means the grapes are only half of what the second oath covered, because the figs part was already taken care of by the קרבן.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabba say:
"An oath that I will not eat figs,"
and then he went back and said:
"An oath that I will not eat figs and grapes,"
and he ate figs, and set aside an offering,
and then he ate grapes —
the grapes count as only a half-measure,
phrases.notes: The figs were already covered by the offering, so the grapes are just half of the 'figs and grapes' oath.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְבִיאִים קׇרְבָּן עַל חֲצִי שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: and one does not bring an offering for a half-measure.
Apparently, where one said:
"An oath that I will not eat figs,"

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר וְאָמַר ״שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכַל תְּאֵנִים וַעֲנָבִים״,
phrases.english: and then said, "An oath that I will not eat figs and grapes,"
since the oath takes effect on the grapes,
it takes effect on the figs as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's explanation from Step 6 that the second oath ('figs and grapes') does not take effect.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the oath 'figs and grapes' after 'figs' does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה treats the grapes as half of the second oath. That means the second oath took hold on the figs too, through מיגו. This is the opposite of what רב הונא said.

steps.title: רב הונא disagrees with רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב הונא does not hold like רבה, so רבה's ruling is no problem for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא does not agree with רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge very simply: רב הונא and רבה just hold differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if רב הונא accepts רבה's מיגו idea. The גמרא says he does not. So for רב הונא, the second oath does not take hold on the figs, and his reading of the משנה still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold that way. He disagrees.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּרַבָּה.
phrases.english: Rav Huna does not hold like Rabba.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּרַבָּה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבה's מיגו ruling was binding on רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא rejects רבה's view, so the second oath does not take hold for him.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא about two נזירות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if someone took two נזירות, finished the first, and then had the first one undone, the second counts in place of the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Someone took two נזירות. He counted the days of the first one and set aside a קרבן. Then he asked to have the first one undone. The second one counts for him in place of the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב הונא again. This step only quotes the source; the next steps work out exactly what case it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes that two נזירות both took effect on this person, since the second one 'fills in' when the first is undone. If that case turns out to be 'נזיר today' said twice, it would go against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow to be a נזיר, usually for thirty days.
He asked a חכם to undo the vow.
It counts for him.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who vowed two terms of naziriteship,
counted the first and set aside an offering,
and asked to be released from it,
phrases.notes: He went to a חכם to undo the first נזירות.

phrases.english: the second counts for him in place of the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבה challenge is answered, the גמרא brings a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that 'נזיר today' said twice does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats two נזירות as both taking effect. The next steps will show its case must be 'today, today'.

steps.title: What case is the ברייתא talking about? Not 'today, tomorrow'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. 'Today, tomorrow' cannot be it, because then the second נזירות would be missing a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he said, 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר tomorrow,' why would the second count in place of the first? There is an extra day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pin down the exact case of the ברייתא. It first suggests 'today, tomorrow' and then rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second נזירות started one day later, its thirty days end one day after the first. So the days he already kept cannot fully cover the second נזירות. That means the ברייתא's ruling cannot fit this case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact facts?
If you say. This introduces a suggestion that will be rejected.
An extra day.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If we say that he said
"I am hereby a nazirite today,
I am hereby a nazirite tomorrow" —
why does the second count for him in place of the first?
There is an extra day!
phrases.notes: The second נזירות began a day later, so it still has one day left that he never kept.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the exact case of the ברייתא quoted in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What wording did the person use for his two נזירות in the ברייתא?
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The second נזירות would have one extra day the first did not cover.

steps.title: The ברייתא must mean 'נזיר today' said twice
steps.stepSummary: Since 'today, tomorrow' does not work, the ברייתא must be talking about someone who said 'נזיר today' twice. This sets up a challenge to רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that he said, 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר today.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes the ברייתא's case is 'נזיר today, נזיר today.' This is a setup for the next move: the ברייתא would then say both נזירות took effect, which seems to go against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With both נזירות starting the same day, the days he kept fit the second נזירות exactly, so it can count in place of the first. But for the second one to count, it had to take effect in the first place. That is just what רב הונא said does not happen.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is obvious. The only option left.
I am hereby a נזיר.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about two נזירות must be talking about 'נזיר today' said twice, and it treats the second one as real. That is about to become a problem for רב הונא.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that he said
"I am hereby a nazirite today,
I am hereby a nazirite today."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting 'today, tomorrow' in Step 10, the גמרא settles on 'today, today'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא's case is someone who said 'נזיר today' twice, which sets up a challenge against רב הונא.
